A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flex3D and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and reconstruction experiments, component ablations, qualitative results, and a user preference study in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, geometry measurements, larger-view evaluations, and qualitative failure analyses.

M1.justification: The view-generation and selection pipeline, camera conditioning, Gaussian decoder, two-stage training, and imperfect-input simulation remain unchanged. Making the MLP explicit in the position equation matches v1's existing procedural description. Appendix A's proposed 4D extensions are future work.

E1.justification: Training retains the internal rendered-object data and Emu-video data; evaluation retains 404 DreamFusion prompts and 947 GSO objects. Additional view configurations and case illustrations concern the existing tasks. The proposed scene and 4D applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 4 add LN3Diff and 3DTopia-XL, extending generation comparisons to direct 3D diffusion while retaining all previous baselines. Section 4.3 also reports comparisons with Gaussian and salt-and-pepper augmentation, without numerical results for those alternatives.

E3.justification: Table 2 adds Chamfer Distance and Normal Correctness evaluation and 24- and 32-view configurations for the full FlexRM model. Section 4.1 specifies single-image conditioning for the new diffusion comparators. Existing dataset sizes, rendering settings, training budgets, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused with/without-selection comparison in Figure 5, failure cases in Appendix E and Figure 9, and a verbal finding that simpler noise augmentations degrade reconstruction. These extend the analysis while retaining the original quantitative ablations in Tables 3–5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both describe the same user-study aggregation: five raters evaluate 40 prompt pairs, with majority preference determining wins.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 1–5 are retained. Table 1 adds LN3Diff results of 0.252/0.234 CLIP/VideoCLIP similarity and a 95% Flex3D win rate, and 3DTopia-XL results of 0.254/0.231 and 97.5%. Table 2 adds geometry scores and 24-/32-view PSNR values of 26.65/26.77. New figures document selection benefits and failures; these are additional results, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the position equation by replacing f(p0) with MLP(f(p0)), distinguishing tri-plane features from the predicted position offset. This is a limited correction to the formal expression; the surrounding position rule and boundedness reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain view curation, flexible Gaussian reconstruction, and robustness training through simulated imperfect inputs. The abstract and conclusion retain the state-of-the-art claims, including the abstract's user-study win rate above 92%; rewritten contribution summaries do not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds specific failure boundaries involving floaters, transparent objects, and thin geometry, attributing thin-geometry selection errors to weak feature matching. Appendix A discusses prospective 3D/4D extensions and initialization of iterative reconstruction. The existing mesh-extraction and large-scene limitations are relocated unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly reports candidate-view generation taking approximately one minute on a single H100 GPU. v3 also identifies the conditioning used for new comparators and cites the geometry-metric protocol. The implementation appendix moves from A to B with its hyperparameters retained; project access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 distinguishes Flex3D from feedback-based methods such as Ouroboros3D, Carve3D, Cycle3D, and IM-3D through modularity, computational cost, and complementary applicability. Additional citations cover distillation, direct diffusion, and Hunyuan3D; the Free3D citation is removed. The broader research framing remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is shortened, contribution and conclusion paragraphs are rewritten, and related-work discussion is expanded. Limitations move into the main text, implementation details are relabeled, and future-research and failure-case appendices are added. Most existing technical prose and its ordering are preserved.

P2.justification: The main paper is extensively reformatted from one column to two, resizing and repositioning figures and compressing tables. Figure 4 gains comparator rows, Tables 1–2 gain rows or columns, and Figures 5 and 9 are new. The original appendix Figures 5–7 remain as Figures 6–8.

improvement.justification: The added direct-diffusion comparisons and geometry measurements strengthen validation, while the selection comparison and failure cases make the method's benefits and limits easier to assess. These provide useful incremental gains for the existing method and benchmarks, with a readability cost from substantially compressed tables.
